Subject: Request for credit calculation after 6/06 incident

Neha,

Thanks for the postmortem published on Monday — appreciate the clear RCA.  Our finance team needs a formal SLA credit calculation and an estimate of the timing/process to apply it to our account.

Quick context: our committed monthly reserved spend is $120,000 (enterprise plan). The outage window you documented (2026-06-06 02:14–05:05 UTC) impacted inference traffic for our customer-facing workflows and generated a billing anomaly. Can you confirm:

- Whether Emerald Health is eligible under Redwood's SLA for a credit for that window
- The math you’ll use to calculate the dollar amount
- A timeline for issuance (account credit vs invoice adjustment) and any paperwork we need to sign

We need this for our internal month-end close. Appreciate a named contact for follow-up.

Best,
Jose

Emerald Health AI

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jose Gomez <j.gomez@emeraldhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for credit calculation after 6/06 incident

Jose — thanks for the note and sorry again for the impact.  Looping in Marissa (billing) and Markus (legal) to get an official calculation and the paperwork path.

Short answer up front: Emerald Health is eligible for a prorated credit under our SLA. Below is our proposed calculation methodology and the information we need from your side to finalize the amount: 

Summary of methodology (proposed)
- SLA baseline: 99.95% monthly availability for the Reserved capacity tier in your contract.
- Billing period used: calendar month (2026-06-01 to 2026-06-30). Total minutes = 43,200.
- Confirmed unavailability window: 2026-06-06 02:14–05:05 UTC = 171 minutes (system measured, includes degraded minutes where requests timed out).
- Pro-rata credit percent = downtime_minutes / total_minutes = 171 / 43200 = 0.003958 (0.3958%)
- Credit calculation = prorate_percent * monthly_reserved_commitment. For your $120,000 monthly commitment: credit = 0.003958 * 120,000 = $474.96 (rounded to $475).

Notes and deviations to expect
- We exclude minutes outside the contract scope (e.g., maintenance windows you opted into). The postmortem timestamps are from our global monitoring; please flag any clock-sync differences on your side.
- For degraded performance that did not cause complete request failure, we include minutes where median latency exceeded the SLA threshold per the contract addendum (that’s already included in our 171-minute window).

Next steps we plan to take
1) Marissa will confirm the line item on an invoice or issue an account credit and create a small credit memo.
2) I’ll prepare a short two-line acknowledgement DocuSign (one-time credit acknowledgement) for Emerald to sign to close the claim.  We use this to mark the account and prevent duplicate claims on the same incident.
3) Markus to confirm legal ok on language (especially around acceptance/offset).

Marissa — can you draft the credit memo and indicate whether we can apply as an invoice adjustment for June or as a post-bill account credit?  Also attaching our working calc in xlsx.

Jose / Sara — I’ve attached the working spreadsheet (emerald_credit_calc_2026-06.xlsx). If those numbers look off to you, tell me which timestamps you want us to re-evaluate and we’ll run the raw logs against your request IDs.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Success — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLA credit reconciliation and payout proposal — Emerald Health incident

Thanks Neha — I reviewed the calc and ran it through finance. Confirming the following operational options for how Emerald wants the payout applied: 

Option A (fastest): Issue account credit of $475 against Emerald’s July billing cycle. Credit will be visible on the account page and will appear as an unapplied credit until used. Expected processing time: 3 business days after signoff.

Option B (invoiced): Apply as a credit memo on the June invoice; this requires a short billing amendment and will reflect on the next statement. Expected processing time: 7–10 business days (depends on invoicing closure).

Per our policy we generate the credit memo once legal confirms the acknowledgement. I prepared a draft DocuSign powerform for a one-time credit acknowledgement (link below). I also attached the finalized Excel with the line-by-line math and ledger mapping:

- Calculations: 171 minutes downtime / 43,200 minutes = 0.3958% of monthly commitment.
- Credit amount: $475 (rounded to nearest dollar per finance rounding rules).

Attachments included:
- emerald_credit_calc_2026-06.xlsx (finalized)
- draft_credit_ack_powerform.pdf (DocuSign preview)

DocuSign link: https://na1.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc-emerald-credit

Jose — which option do you prefer (A or B)? If A, I’ll queue the credit and we’ll send the acknowledgment form for signature.

Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
